items.text: After Croatia introduced the euro on January 1, 2023, Croatians are anxious about a sharp increase in prices. The prices of goods increased by at least 30%, and people are looking for new jobs to cope. In January, traders began to round prices from the local currency, and most increased. The government threatened sanctions unless traders lowered prices; however, traders blamed inflation and the growing cost of raw materials and energy. The president of the country’s Consumers’ Association said they observed the prices after January 1, 2023. Energy, oil, electricity, and water prices had no change in the previous two months; however, when the country switched to the euro, the prices went wild, and they continued to rise every day between five to twenty percent, depending on the product. Over a two-week period, inspectors found about 40% of businesses hiked prices unjustifiably , and they gave fines that totaled more than 250,000 dollars. Difficult words: inflation (an increase in prices and a fall in the value of money), hike (to grow), unjustifiably (in a way that can’t be accepted). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

On January 1, 2023, Croatia started to use the euro, and then the prices of almost all products went up. Many people are upset about the situation, and some of them had to find an extra job. In January, traders rounded prices, and for most products, prices went up by five to twenty percent. Traders said that the reasons were the rise in prices of materials and energy, but oil, electricity, and water didn’t change in the previous two months. Inspectors checked hundreds of businesses in January, and they found that 40% of them increased prices too much. Traders used the situation to increase prices more than they should. The government said that traders had to cut prices or they would face sanctions . Difficult words: round (to change the price to the closest number), inspector (a person whose job is to check if people follow rules), sanction (money which someone pays if he breaks a law or rule). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

On January 1, 2023, Croatia starts to use the euro. Everything is more expensive now. The prices of all products go up by five to twenty percent. Some things cost 30% more than in December. These changes are very big. People are upset. Some people must find a second job. Sellers say that materials and energy is more expensive. The situation is not true. The prices do not go up in the last two months. Some traders use the euro to increase prices. Inspectors check hundreds of businesses. Inspectors find that 40% of businesses increase prices too much. The government asks them to lower prices. They will pay a fine if they don’t. Difficult words: increase (to make something bigger or greater), inspector (a person who checks if people follow rules), fine (money which someone must pay if he breaks a rule). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Visibly emotional, New Zealand’s Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern announced she was stepping down ahead of a general election for later this year. The 42-year-old said she lacked the energy or inspiration to seek re-election, and so her term as prime minister would conclude by the 7 th of February, 2023. She also said she was stepping down because others could do the job better. In 2017, Ardern became the world’s youngest female leader when she led her Labor Party to power. During her stunning political career, she led the country through unprecedented crises, and she became a torch-bearer for liberal values across the world. She won international praise and admiration for her responses to the Christchurch mass shooting, the 2019 fatal volcanic eruption, and the control of the COVID-19 pandemic. Arden’s announcement came as a huge surprise and no successor is apparent. Difficult words: unprecedented (never done or known before), torch-bearer (a leader in a campaign or movement), successor (a person that follows or takes the job after someone else). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

On Thursday, New Zealand’s Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern announced that she would resign before the 7 th of February, 2023. The news surprised everyone because she was one of the most successful leaders of the country. Ardern is 42 years old, and during her term of five and a half years, she gave birth to a girl. She said that she had too little energy to continue the job, and she believed that someone else could do it better. During her career, Ardern responded to the Christchurch mass shooting , the 2019 volcano eruption, and the COVID-19 pandemic. Difficult words: announce (to say something in public), resign (to officially leave a job), mass shooting (an incident when an attacker kills people with a gun). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Jacinda Ardern is the prime minister of New Zealand. She is in the job since 2017. She becomes a mother in 2018. Last week, Ardern says that she will stop her job. She does not have enough energy. She believes that someone else can do the job better. The news surprises everyone. Right now, people aren’t sure who will be the next prime minister. Ardern is one of the best leaders of the country. She deals with many difficult situations. For example, she deals with a mass shooting in Christchurch, a volcano eruption , and the coronavirus. Difficult words: prime minister (the leader of a government), mass shooting (when a person kills many people with a gun), volcano eruption (when a mountain explodes). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A high-tech Bosnian dairy farm is among the first to turn animal waste into electricity. Spreca Farm is becoming self-reliant with biogas from animal waste and silage , even as high energy prices threaten the subsidy -dependent agriculture industry. The biogas plant produces electricity from renewable energy sources in a process of several stages, a mixing pit, fermenters with mixers, storage for the biogas, and engines for power generation. Extra thermal energy heats some farm buildings. The project can produce more electricity in an hour than the average household’s monthly consumption. Once the plant is fully operational, it’ll be able to produce 600 kilowatts per hour. Difficult words: biogas (gas from natural sources), silage (grass and other green plants that are cut and stored to feed cattle), subsidy (money from the government to help an industry or business). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Spreca Farm in Bosnia is one of the first in the country to make electricity from animal waste. Many farms depend on government subsidies , but energy prices are growing fast, and farmers are looking to save money. The electric factory makes biogas from animal waste and silage, which is grass and plants that cows eat. The factory has several parts: it mixes the waste and silage and then fermentation creates biogas. Some heat from fermentation warms some farm buildings. The factory makes more electricity in one hour than one family needs in one month. Farmers can become independent from government help. Difficult words: subsidy (money from the government to support a business), biogas (a gas which from changing food or animal waste) fermentation (a chemical process during which bacteria make changes in a thing). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Spreca is a farm in Bosnia. This farm is special. It is one of the first farms to use modern technologies . The farm makes biogas. Biogas is a gas that comes fermentation. During fermentation, bacteria make food or animal waste . Fermentation also makes heat. Farmers use some of heat for farm buildings. Farms get some money from the government. Power is getting more expensive. Farmers look to save money. They become more independent with biogas. Difficult words: technology (machines and processes), bacterium (a very small living animals; bacteria are many bacterium), animal waste (leftover food which leave the animal’s body). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The mayor of Amiens, France, appealed to the singer Madonna to loan the city a painting that she allegedly recently purchased. In a video appeal, Brigitte Fouré said that the early 19th-century painting is by Jérome-Martin Langlois called Diana and Endymion. It once hung in the local museum and the Louvre lent it to Amiens; however, the painting was lost without trace during World War I. The mayor clarified she didn’t dispute the singer’s legal acquisition ; however, Amiens was a candidate to be the European capital of culture for 2028. On this occasion, she asked Madonna to lend the city her painting, so that the inhabitants could rediscover this work and enjoy it. Difficult words: without trace (without any evidence where someone or something is), dispute (to argue about something), acquisition (buy or get something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The mayor of Amiens, France, made an official appeal to the singer Madonna. The mayor said that the painting once hung in the local museum. The name of the work was Diana and Endymion, and Jérome-Martin Langlois painted it in the 19 th century. Before World War I, the Louvre Museum lent the painting to Amiens, but during the war, the work was lost. For many years, nobody knew where the painting was. The mayor said that Amiens was a candidate for the European capital of culture for 2028. She said if Madonna could lend the painting to Amiens in 2028, the situation would be great. Local people could also discover it again. Difficult words: appeal (to ask formally), candidate (a person or thing which competes to get something), discover (to find). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The mayor of Amiens, France, makes a video. In the video, she speaks to the singer Madonna. In the 19 th century, Jérome-Martin Langlois makes a painting. The painting is called Diana and Endymion. It is in the Louvre Museum in Paris. The Louvre lends it to Amiens before World War I. Then the painting gets lost during the war. Nobody knows where it is. Recently , Madonna buys the painting. Amiens wants to be the European capital of culture in 2028. The mayor wishes to borrow the painting from Madonna. The mayor says that local people could enjoy the painting. It is the city’s painting in the past. Difficult words: mayor (the leader of a town or city), recently (not long ago), borrow (to take something that belongs to somebody else and give it back later). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Locals of a small Chinese town in Yunnan Province got a bit of a shock when a wild elephant wandered downtown . Authorities followed the large mammal ’s every movement. The elephant eventually left the town, but the locals will probably never forget this special visit. Difficult words: wander (walk slowly around), downtown (a city centre), mammal (a warm-blooded animal; babies are born from their mother’s body and not in eggs; the mother gives her babies milk). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A wild elephant wandered into a small town in China. Authorities followed its every move. It left the town eventually , but the people will never forget its visit. Difficult words: wander (walk slowly around), authorities (the police, for example), eventually (in the end). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is from a town in China. A wild elephant goes into a small town. Authorities watch it. They go where it goes. In the end, the elephant leaves. However, people will not forget it. Difficult words: wild (free, not from a zoo), authorities (the police, for example), will (in the future). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Mitsi the cat, who lives at a train station near Tel Aviv, Israel, became a viral sensation . She can be seen lying around the station or calmly resting upon a ticket gate as commuters make their way through. She may bring calm, peace or a smile to a lot of people, but she cannot stay. Some people are scared of animals or have allergies. The station manager said that people are looking for a home for Mitsi where she would be looked after the same way that she is at the station. Difficult words: viral (quickly happening), sensation (a very popular thing, usually on the Internet), commuter (a person who commutes – travels to work or school). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Mitsi is a cat who lives at a train station near Tel Aviv, Israel. You can see her lying around the station or calmly resting upon a ticket gate. She became popular with the people at the station, as well as the Internet. To many commuters , she brings good feelings like peace and calm. However, some people can be afraid of animals, or have allergies. That is why the station manager is looking for a home for Mitsi. Difficult words: commuter (a person who commutes – travels to work or school), peace (the feeling that everything is OK), calm (being quiet and happy. You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Mitsi is a cat. She lives at a station in Israel. She lies around the station. She watches people. She sits on ticket gates . Many people like her. She makes them feel good. However, some people do not like cats. They are afraid of them. They can also be allergic to cats. The station manager knows this. He wants everyone to be happy. He is looking for a home for Mitsi. Difficult words: ticket gates (a little ‘wall’ which lets you go through only if you have a ticket), allergic to (if you are allergic to something, your body starts to feel bad – your eyes can be red, your skin can be red, you cannot take in air well…). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

According to several media reports, Microsoft plans to cut thousands of jobs. After Amazon and Meta’s recent job cuts announcements, the expected Microsoft layoffs are the latest in the US technology sector. Amid a worsening global economic outlook, Microsoft reportedly plans to cut about five percent or its workforce, or about 11,000 people. The jobs will be cut in engineering and human resources divisions. Microsoft is under pressure to maintain growth rates after several quarters of downturn in the personal computer market. According to analysts, the tech sector is struggling from slower demand and will cut jobs. Difficult words: layoff (end a worker’s job because of economic conditions or less work), downturn (a decline in business and economic activity). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Last week, several media reports said that the US tech company Microsoft planned to cut thousands of jobs. Recently, Amazon and Meta announced job cuts because of the worsening economic situation. Microsoft will probably cut about 11,000 people, which is five percent of all its employees. The job cuts will be in engineering and human resources departments. The lower demand for personal computers led to lower results for Microsoft. Experts expect more job cuts in the tech sector . Difficult words: human resources (the department of a company that hires and trains new employees), demand (when many people want to buy something), tech sector (companies which sell computers, electronics, and software). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Reports say that Microsoft will cut thousands of jobs. Many people will leave the company. In recent years, the demand for computers is lower. People do not buy many computers. This news is bad for Microsoft. Its business is not very good. The company must save money. Reports say that 11,000 Microsoft workers will lose their jobs. Problems in the tech sector are happening. Other big companies cut jobs, too. These companies are Meta and Amazon. They plan for a worse economic situation. They must save money, too. Difficult words: cut (to lose or drop), demand (when many people want to buy something), tech sector (companies which sell computers and electronics). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

On Monday, Italian actress Gina Lollobrigida died at the age of 95. Lollobrigida was born in Subiaco, Italy, and as a teenager, she entered beauty contests. In 1947, she placed third in the Miss Italia pageant . During the 1950s, she achieved international film stardom, and she was dubbed the most beautiful woman in the world. Lollobrigida starred in a large number of European and American films, including a Bafta-winning ‘Bread, Love and Dreams’. In 1953, her performance in ‘Beat the Devil’ brought her international fame; she played opposite Humphrey Bogart. At the height of her fame, she was known simply as ‘La Lollo’; she was an internationally recognized epitome of Italian post-war cinema, rivaled only by Sophia Loren. When Lollobrigida stopped making films, she developed new careers as a photographer, sculptor, and a UNICEF goodwill ambassador . In 2018, she received a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame. Difficult words: pageant (a beauty contest), epitome (a typical or ideal example), goodwill ambassador (a person who travels to different places to promote friendship and kindness). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

On Monday, Italian actress Gina Lollobrigida died in Rome at 95 years old. As a teenager, Lollobrigida took part in beauty contests , and when she was 20 years old, she was third in Miss Italy. She played in many European and American films. In the 1950s, she became very popular, especially after she starred in ‘Beat the Devil’ with Humphrey Bogart. She was married to a Yugoslavian doctor for 22 years and they had one son. When Lollobrigida stopped making films in 1997, she became a photographer and sculptor, worked in fashion and cosmetics companies, and was a UNICEF goodwill ambassador . Difficult words: beauty contest (a competition in which the winner is the most beautiful person), star (to play in a movie), goodwill ambassador (a person who travels to other countries to support good ideas). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Gina Lollobrigida is an Italian actress. She dies in Rome on Monday. She is 95 years old. Lollobrigida is born in Subiaco in 1927. As a young woman, she is a model. She gets third place in Miss Italy in 1947. She becomes famous in the 1950s. She plays in many Europeans and American films. One of her biggest roles is in the film ‘Beat the Devil’. She plays with actor Humphrey Bogart in the film. Lollobrigida stops making films in 1997. She becomes a photographer and sculptor . She also works for fashion and makeup companies. She is a UNICEF ambassador . She is married to a Yugoslavian doctor for 22 years. They have one son together. Difficult words: role (an actor’s part in a play or film), sculptor (an artist who makes objects from wood, clay, or stone), ambassador (a person who works for a country or organization in another country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Thousands of climate activists demonstrated against the clearance and demolition of the Luezerath Village in West Germany. The regional and national governments both include the Green party; they reached a deal with utility company RWE to destroy the village in order to expand a coal mine. They argued that coal was needed to ensure Germany’s energy security after less gas supplies from Russia. The Green party said that the deal fulfilled several of the environmentalists’ demands and saved five other villages. However, environmentalists rejected this deal, and they said that bulldozing the village would result in vast amounts of greenhouse gas emissions. Then Germany couldn’t meet its commitments under the 2015 Paris Agreement. Greta Thunberg was among the protesters. She said that Germany was one of the biggest polluters in the world and needed to be held accountable . Difficult words: utility company (a company that supplies electricity, gas, or water to the public), accountable (responsible). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Thousands of people protested in West Germany against the demolition of a village. The Luezerath Village is on the edge of a coal mine, which the government plans to expand. Last year, the government and utility company RWE made a deal. They said that they had to expand the mine because Germany needed independence from Russian gas. The government said that the original plan was to demolish five villages. Germany is one of Europe’s biggest polluters . Protesters said that demolition of the village would make too many emissions, and Germany wouldn’t reach its goal in the 2015 Paris Agreement. Difficult words: demolition (destruction of a building or other structure), utility company (a company which gets electricity, gas, or water to buildings), polluter (a person or organization which makes the air, water, or land dirty or damaged). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Thousands of people protest in West Germany. The government wants to destroy a village. The name of the village is Luezerath. It is very close to a coal mine . The government wants to make the mine larger. Germany needs more coal. The country still depends on coal from Russia. Protesters say that Germany is one of the biggest polluters in Europe. A polluter makes a lot of trash or smoke. Germany must be responsible. The country must reach its goal of the 2015 Paris Agreement. Difficult words: destroy (to break into many pieces), coal (a black or brown rock which burns easily), mine (a place where people get rock or minerals from under the ground). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Donald Trump’s real estate company was ordered to pay a 1.61-million-dollar criminal penalty after a court convicted it of a 15-year-scheme to defraud tax authorities. According to state law, the penalty was the maximum possible that the court could use, and the penalty was no surprise. However, it may impact other business, because it’ll be a problem for lenders. Alan Weisselberg worked for Trump’s family for 50 years and was the company’s former CFO. Last week, the court sentenced him to five months in prison after they found him guilty of 15 criminal charges including criminal tax fraud and falsified business records. Trump called the charges part of a witch hunt by democrats who dislike him in his politics, and his company plans to appeal. Difficult words: defraud (to illegally take money from a person or company), falsify (to change documents or numbers), witch hunt (a campaign directed against a person or group considered dangerous and whose opinions are unpopular). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Last week, a New York judge sentenced Donald Trump’s real estate company to pay a penalty of 1.61 million dollars. According to the judge, the company avoided paying taxes, and the penalty was the highest which the company could get. Experts said that the verdict could have a negative impact on the company because other companies would not want to lend it money. Trump said that he didn’t agree with the penalty, and the Democratic Party wanted to hurt him and his business. His company plans to appeal to a higher court to change the verdict. Difficult words: penalty (the money someone has to pay when he breaks a law), avoid (to not do something), verdict (a decision of a judge). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Donald Trump has a real estate company. A real estate company buys, sells, or rents buildings. Last week, the company gets a penalty of 1.61 million dollars. It is the highest penalty which is possible. The reason is the company cheats in paying taxes . It happens for 15 years. Experts say that this penalty could be bad for other companies. They lend money to this company. Maybe, they will stop. Trump says that some people want to hurt his business. They want to hurt him as a person. He does not want to pay the penalty. His company will go to another court. They will ask to change the situation. Difficult words: penalty (the money which someone pays if he doesn’t follow a law), cheat (to make someone believe something is or is not true), tax (money which people and companies pay to the government). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

US president Biden approved an emergency declaration for California, as it struggles to cope with a series of deadly storms. Since December 26, 2022, a series of storms killed at least 19 people and brought floods, power outages , mudslides, evacuations, and road closures. Some areas had floods three times in ten days. The president’s action makes federal funding available to affected people in Merced, Sacramento, and Santa Cruz counties . Biden also approved an emergency declaration for Alabama on Sunday. At least five tornadoes hit central Alabama on Thursday. At least nine people died in tornadoes; they destroyed homes and stopped power to tens of thousands in the southeast United States. Difficult words: outage (a time when a power supply or other service isn’t available), federal funding (money that a government uses for a specific purpose), county (a large area in a state). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Since the end of December, California fought with rainstorms. The storms brought floods and mudslides, and in some areas, three floods happened in ten days. The floods destroyed infrastructure , and authorities closed some roads. Thousands of people were without power, or they had to leave their homes. The US president declared an emergency in California, which will provide financial help to the people who need it the most. Since Sunday, a state of emergency is also in Alabama where at least five tornadoes hit the state, and nine people died. Difficult words: infrastructure (roads, bridges, electricity network, and so on), declare (to say something officially or openly), provide (to give). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Heavy rainstorms hit California in December 2022. Since that time, the US state fights with floods and mudslides . In some places, three floods happen in ten days. The situation is very bad. Thousands of people must leave their homes. Floods destroy roads and power lines . Some people are without electricity. Authorities close roads. The US president declares a state of emergency. The action lets the government control the situation. People can get help from the government. The help is very important. An emergency is also in Alabama. Several tornadoes hit the state on Thursday. Nine people die. Difficult words: mudslide (when mud, stones, and other things fall down a hill or mountain), power line (a cable which gets electricity to buildings), declare (to say something officially and openly). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Swedish government’s company LKAB says that it has identified mineral resources of more than one million tons of rare earth minerals in the Kiruna area. The discovery is the largest known such deposit in Europe in the far north of Sweden. Rare earth minerals are essential to many high-tech manufacturing processes, and people use them in electric vehicles, wind turbines, portable electronics, microphones, and speakers. People currently do not mine them in Europe, so the region depends on imports from elsewhere. The demand for rare minerals is expected to rise in coming years due to an increase in electric vehicles and renewable energy. According to the Swedish Minister for Energy, Business, and Industry, mines will bring the EU’s self-sufficiency and independence from Russia and China. Europe will reduce its carbon footprint and strengthen its competitiveness at the same time. Difficult words: essential (extremely important), self-sufficiency (care for everything without the help of other people or countries), competitiveness (do business better than other companies). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Swedish company LKAB found more than one million tons of rare minerals in the north of the country. No other deposit of these minerals exists in Europe, and Europe fully depends on China and Russia for them. These minerals are necessary to make electric cars, wind turbines, and electronics, and the global demand for them is growing. When the new mine opens, everything will change for people there. Europe will become self-sufficient , and it will make these products with much less transportation and pollution. Difficult words: rare (unusual), deposit (a natural underground area of rock or minerals), self-sufficient (be independent from anything or anyone). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Minerals are special rocks. People use them to make things. A Swedish government company finds many minerals. They are in the north of Sweden. More than one million tons of the minerals are underground. These minerals are rare. Rare is a small amount of them in the world. Before, Europe must buy them from China and Russia. People need these minerals to make electric cars, wind turbines , and electronics. The deposit in Sweden is the first in Europe. When the mining starts, Europe will be more independent. The work will also be more friendly to the natural world. Difficult words: wind turbine (a big device which changes wind power into electricity), deposit (a lot of rock or minerals in the ground), mine (to get coal or other minerals from the ground). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Columbian authorities are melting down around 29,000 weapons; they confiscated them in operations against criminal organizations, and they are turning them into steel to build low-income housing. Among the seized weapons were riffles, machine guns, and rocket launchers. During the melting process, a part will be turned into steel for construction rods. A member of the Colombian Armed Forces said that he considered this act virtuous . Criminals had harmful elements in Colombia’s streets, and now they will have a virtuous end. Difficult words: confiscate (to officially take someone’s property), virtuous (good moral qualities and behavior), element (a bad or good thing). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

During operations against criminals, authorities in Colombia seized more than 29,000 guns. Now, they are turning these guns into steel. Among the guns were riffles, machine guns, and rocket launchers . Criminals used them to kill people in the streets of Colombia. Workers are melting these guns to make steel. They will use the metal to build houses for people with low income . One Colombian soldier said that things which once hurt people would now help people. Difficult words: seize (to take something and keep it), rocket launcher (a tube which fires a rocket), income (money which a person gets for work). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Authorities in Colombia seize more than 29,000 guns. These guns belong to criminals. Criminals kill people with these guns. Workers melt the guns. They heat them. They turn them into steel . They use this steel to build houses. People with low income will live in these houses. One soldier says that he is very happy about the work. It is important. Something that kills people instead will help them. Difficult words: seize (to take something and keep it), steel (a strong grey metal which people use to build things), income (money which a person gets for work). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Workers carry out and supervise emergency cleaning and repairs on Paris’s sewage system; they aren’t happy with the French government’s plan to make them work longer. Last week, Prime Minister Elisabeth Borne announced that in 2027, the workers need to work for 43 years to get a full pension, and she said that this change was necessary to balance the accounts. To sewer cleaners, this change is a long time because this profession is dangerous and causes physical problems. They crouch in dark tunnels filled with overflowing fecal matter and rats. The workers plan to take part in a nationwide strike on January 19, 2023, to stop the reform . Difficult words: crouch (to bend the knees and lover the body close to the ground), fecal matter (solid remains of food that leave the body), reform (a change in a law, job, or other organizational matter). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Last week, the French government introduced its pension reform . According to the change, people will have to work 43 years to get a full pension. Workers of the Paris sewage system don’t agree with the reform, and they plan to take part in a national strike on January 19, 2023. Their work is very demanding and dangerous, too. They clean and repair the city’s sewage system, so they walk through long dark tunnels, often on their knees. The tunnels are full of feces and rats. Some workers said that they couldn’t imagine working longer because they were very tired. They hope that the government will not pass the law. Difficult words: reform (changes to a law), sewage system (a system which takes dirty water from homes and businesses), feces (food waste which leaves the body). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A pension is money from the government to people. These people do not work anymore. They must work for some years to get pension. The French government plans to change the pension system. People will have to work longer to get a full pension. Some people are angry. They will take part in a national strike on January 19, 2023. Sewage cleaners are very unhappy about the change. They work in sewage tunnels. They clean and fix the sewage system. The tunnels are full of feces and rats. Their work is very hard and dangerous. They do not want to work longer. Difficult words: national strike (when many people in a country stop their work and protest in the streets), sewage (dirty water from homes and factories), feces (food waste which leaves the body). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Islamic GPS app, which launched in 2016, finds mosques and centres to pray at in just a tap. It aims at Muslim travellers on holiday or on hajj pilgrimages , and the co-founder of Muslamic Makers said that it is basically like having the religion in your pocket . Difficult words: hajj (the greater Muslim pilgrimage to Mecca), pilgrimage (a journey to an important religious place), in your pocket (in very tiny form because your phone can go in your pocket). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

There is an app for Muslims that launched in 2016 to find mosques and centres to pray at in just a tap. The app aims at Muslim travellers on holiday or on hajj pilgrimages . The co-founder said that it ‘puts the religion in your pocket’. Difficult words: launch (start), hajj (the greater Muslim pilgrimage to Mecca), pilgrimage (a journey to an important religious place), co-founder (a person who co-founds – starts a company together with someone). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

There is an app for Muslims. People launch it in 2016. It finds mosques and centres to pray . It is for Muslim travellers. The co-founder says that it ‘puts Islam in your pocket’. Difficult words: launch (start), pray (think, meditate, talk to god), co-founder (a person who co-founds – starts a company together with someone). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Companies including GM, Ford, and Google say that they want to work together to scale up the use of virtual power plants (VPPs). People describe virtual power plants as a cleaner and greener way to avoid blackouts, and they could be one solution to a looming global energy crisis. VPPs are pools of decentralized energy resources such as electric vehicles or electric heaters controlled by smart thermostats. With customers’ permission, VPPs will use advanced software to react to electricity shortages when they switch off unnecessary energy consumption of resources. For example, they will switch thousands of electrical vehicles from charge to discharge mode or prompt electrical heaters to lower their output. VPPS have already improved grid reliability in places like Germany and Australia. Thanks to new or enlarged tax incentives for sustainable energy efforts, experts expect explosive growth in the United States, as well. Difficult words: scale up (to increase something), looming (about to happen soon and causing worry), incentive (a thing that motivates someone to do something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Some of the biggest companies such as GM, Ford, or Google are trying to solve the global energy crisis . They are working together to increase the use of virtual power plants. Virtual power plants use modern software to reduce energy consumption of some electric appliances such as heaters or cars. The software knows if a shortage of electricity is happening, and it can switch the appliances off. Virtual power plants already work well in Germany and Australia, and experts believe that they will become very popular in United States, too. Difficult words: energy crisis (not enough electricity in a country or region), virtual (something that exists only in a computer), shortage (the situation when things are lacking). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Experts want to solve the energy crisis. Virtual power plants could be a clean way to stop blackouts. A blackout is when city or country doesn’t have enough electricity. Blackouts happen more often. People need too much energy. Virtual power plants use modern software. This software sees if enough electricity is in the grid . If not, the software can turn off or reduce power to things. They can be heaters or electric cars. Virtual power plants already work well in Germany and Australia. Experts hope that they will become popular in the United States, too. Difficult words: virtual (only in a computer), grid (a network of cables which distribute electricity), reduce (to make something smaller or less in amount). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A six-year-old boy shot a teacher at Richneck Elementary School in Virginia, United States. 25-year-old Abigail Zwerner was shot through her hand, and the bullet landed in her chest. She’s currently in stable condition at a local hospital. The boy brought the gun to the school and fired it in the class; he is held in emergency custody and temporary detention order. Although authorities said the shooting wasn’t accidental, it may not be prosecuted as a crime. For any person to stand a trial, they must be capable of criminal intent ; the law generally recognizes that ability at 7 years old. Also, the child has to understand the nature of the proceedings, be able to assist his lawyer, understand the role of a judge and a prosecutor, and understand his own rights. Julie McConnell is a lawyer and the director of the Children’s Defense Clinic at the University of Richmond; she said a 6-year-old child would never be able to understand such complex legal factors. According to police, the boy’s mother had legally purchased the firearm, and she could face charges for criminal negligence . Difficult words: detention (the arrest or imprisonment of someone), intent (intention or purpose), negligence (failure to take proper care). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Last week, a six-year-old boy brought a gun to school, and he shot his teacher. The incident happened at an elementary school in Virginia, United States, and police said that it was not an accident. The boy pointed the gun at the teacher, and he shot her in the hand and chest. Luckily, the 25-year-old woman survived and she is in stable condition at a hospital. The law says that a 7-year-old child is able to understand what a crime is. According to a lawyer from the University of Richmond, a child needs to understand who a judge and a prosecutor are, how a trial works, and he also needs to know his rights. A child who is only six years old can’t understand all these things. The boy is in custody now, and it is possible that his mother will face charges because she bought the gun. Difficult words: stable condition (when someone’s health is not likely to get worse), prosecutor (a lawyer who works for the government, and he tries to prove that someone did something wrong), face charges (to be officially accused of a crime). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Virginia, United States, a boy shoots his teacher. The boy is only six years old. The boy brings the gun to school. The gun belongs to his mother. The boy points the gun at the teacher. He shoots the woman in the hand and chest. The teacher is in a hospital now. Police say that the shooting is not an accident. The boy wants to hurt the woman. Laws say that a six-year-old child does not understand what a crime is. The boy is now in custody . Authorities must decide what to do. The boy is too young to have a trial . He must work with his lawyer. He must know his rights, too. Authorities will probably accuse his mother of a crime. Difficult words: in custody (when an authority cares for a child), trial (a formal law event with someone who does something wrong), accuse (to say that someone does something wrong). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Two Ebola outbreaks and waves of rebel conflicts struck Beni in Democratic Republic of Congo. However, they haven’t stopped production at a popular local beer factory. The factory is located in North Kivu. It is an impoverished province that has been grappling with major fights by the M23 Rebel group. The company employs hundreds of workers, which is a big deal in a country where 73% of the people live on less than 1.9 dollars a day. Many people joined the factory, and it has become their only hope to make money. The plant cost 134 million dollars, and the output tripled to 600,000 hectoliters between 2013 and 2021. Last year, the company expanded; however, workers sometimes must pass rebel checkpoints to deliver along roads, or poorly maintained roads are difficult to travel. This situation lengthens the supply time for some areas, and sometimes it prevents deliveries. Difficult words: impoverished (poor or weakened), grapple (to struggle), checkpoint (a place where people are stopped and checked). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A French company built a beer factory in Beni, Democratic Republic of Congo. Two Ebola outbreaks and rebel violence didn’t stop the beer, but the factory is facing many problems. Congo is a poor country, and for many people, the factory is their only hope to earn some money. 73% of people live on less than 1.9 dollars a day. Between 2013 and 2021, the factory’s output tripled, and last year, it made 600,000 hectoliters of beer. The company built a second filling line , but workers struggle to deliver beer to some areas. Some roads are in a very bad state, and they are dangerous because of the rebel groups. Difficult words: outbreak (a sudden start to something unpleasant, for example, a war or disease), output (how much a company or machine makes), filling line (a part of a factory where a machine fills bottles). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Congo is a poor country. Most people live on less than 2 dollars a day. A French company builds a beer factory in Beni. The factory is very important for local people. Many of them work there. Between 2013 and 2021, the production of beer grows. Last year, the company builds a second filling line . There are problems with rebel groups . The area is dangerous. Workers cannot deliver beer to some places. Also, some roads are very bad. It takes a long time to get beer to some places. Difficult words: production (when you make things), filling line (a part of a factory where a machine fills bottles), rebel group (people who fight against the government). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Prince Harry’s memoir became the UK’s fastest selling non-fiction book. Harry’s book garnered global attention with its disclosures about his personal struggles and its accusations about other royals, including his father King Charles, stepmother Camilla, and elder brother Prince William. According to the publisher, 400,000 copies have been sold so far across hardback, e-book, and audio formats. Last Thursday, extracts from the book leaked when its Spanish language edition went on sale early by mistake in Spain. In the book, Harry speaks of his grief and life after the death of his mother Princess Diana when he was just 12 years old, his use of cocaine and other drugs to cope, and how he killed 25 Taliban fighters while serving as a soldier in Afghanistan. He also revealed a fight with his brother and how they both begged his father not to marry Camilla. They wed in 2005, and she is not the queen consort . Difficult words: garner (to get), disclosure (information or something known), queen consort (a king’s wife). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

This week, Prince Harry’s memoir went on sale, and it quickly became one of the UK’s fastest-selling books. The publisher said that 400,000 copies of the book sold already, and people waited in lines to get their copy on the first day of sale. In the book, Harry speaks about the death of his mother Princess Diana; she died in a car crash when he was only 12 years old. He speaks about drug use to feel better after his mother’s death, and also about killing people as a soldier in Afghanistan. In the book, Harry gives many details about the relationship with his brother Prince William and also about other members of the royal family. So far, the royal family hasn’t commented . Difficult words: memoir (a book about your life), publisher (a company that sells work such as books or music), comment (to say your opinions about something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Prince Harry belongs to the British royal family. He is the younger son of King Charles. His brother is Prince William. Harry writes a book about his life. The week, the book is in shops. It sells very fast in the UK. People buy 400,000 copies already. Harry writes about when his mother Princess Diana dies. He is only 12 years old when it happens. Her death is very hard for him. He takes drugs to feel better. Later, Harry is a soldier. He fights in Afghanistan. He kills 25 people there. Harry also speaks about problems with his brother and stepmother Camilla. The royal family do not say what they think about the book. Difficult words: copy (one book, magazine, newspaper, or other work), stepmother (a woman who is married to someone’s father, but she is not the original mother of the person). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This January, temperatures across Europe reached an all-time high. Many nations are suffering from a warmer winter. For example, in Bosnia, the exceptionally warm weather prompted tourism authorities to consider a declaration of a natural emergency. In Switzerland, Alpine slopes lack the blanket of snow needed to ski. In Macedonia, low snow has kept away thousands of tourists from ski resorts. In Bilbao, Spain, the temperature reached 25.1 degrees Celsius, which was 10 degrees more than average for this time of year. According to scientists, extreme weather events are more frequent, more intense, and last longer because of human- induced climate change. Experts forecast the above-normal temperatures to last until mid-January. Difficult words: prompt (to lead to something), induce (to cause). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

2022 was the second-warmest year in Europe since 1950, and this winter is the hottest in history. A warm winter has a bad impact on many countries which depend on tourism. Switzerland and Macedonia have big problems because no snow is on the slopes for skiers. Bilbao, Spain’s temperature reached 25 degrees Celsius last week, which was 10 degrees higher than normal in winter. Scientists say that people are causing climate change, and climate change is causing extreme weather events. Droughts or floods happen more often, they are more intense , and they also last longer. Difficult words: slope (a place on a hill or mountain where people ski), drought (a long period of time without rain), intense (very great or strong). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Our world is getting warmer. 2022 is the second-warmest year in Europe. The other warmest year is 1950. This year’s winter is the warmest ever. A warm winter stops snow in the mountains. Countries like Switzerland, Austria, Macedonia, or Italy need tourists. They don’t come. Macedonia is full of skiers in winter. The mountains are without skiers. Spain is unusually warm, too. Bilbao is 25 degrees Celsius last week. The heat is 10 degrees more than usual. The weather is becoming more extreme . More fires, floods , and droughts happen. Experts say that such unusual weather will be usual in the future. Difficult words: extreme (very great or unusual), flood (a time when water gets into buildings and homes), drought (a long time without rain). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.
